title: Field-Space Entanglement Dynamics Between Tunnel-Coupled Luttinger Liquids
authors: Léonce Dupays, Taufiq Murtadho, Bi Hong Tiang, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Paola Ruggiero
abstract: Entanglement dynamics depend not only on how a quantum system is partitioned, but critically on how interactions across that partition are structured. For a spatial bipartition of a locally interacting system, entanglement is generated near the boundary and then propagates into the bulk. By contrast, when two extended quantum fields are coupled locally along their entire length, the interaction crosses the field-space partition everywhere, and this generates correlations throughout the system. Here, we study the entanglement dynamics between two gapless one-dimensional quantum many-body systems described by Luttinger liquid theory. The systems are initially decoupled and prepared at zero or finite temperature, after which a time-dependent tunneling interaction is activated uniformly along their length. Within a Gaussian approximation, we derive general analytical expressions for the logarithmic negativity, mutual information, and Rényi entropies under arbitrary coupling protocols. At zero temperature, entanglement displays an early-time power-law growth whose exponent is fixed solely by the first non-null derivative of the tunneling protocol. Once the coupling saturates, we obtain exact long-time averages of the information-theoretic quantities and characterise how the correlations scale with temperature and the final coupling strength. We also analyse how mutual information and logarithmic negativity approach the adiabatic limit for a very slow protocol with respect to intrinsic system timescale. This work extends the study of entanglement dynamics in nonequilibrium field theory to field-space partitions and mixed initial states.
summary: This paper analyzes the field-space entanglement dynamics between two coupled Luttinger liquids subjected to a time-varying tunneling interaction. Using Gaussian approximations and solving the Ermakov equation for each momentum mode, the authors derive analytical expressions for key entanglement measures like logarithmic negativity. The results characterize how correlations build up over time, providing insights into non-equilibrium quantum information transfer.
main_problem: The study focuses on how entanglement dynamics evolve between two extended quantum fields when a time-dependent tunneling interaction is activated across their entire length, contrasting with standard spatial bipartitions.
main_result: Analytical expressions for logarithmic negativity and mutual information are derived in the Gaussian approximation, showing that early-time entanglement growth exponents depend only on the first non-null derivative of the coupling protocol.
method: The analysis employs a Gaussian approximation after transforming the Hamiltonian into symmetric and antisymmetric field sectors. Key results rely on solving the mode-dependent Ermakov equation for each momentum mode.
model_or_system: The system consists of two gapless one-dimensional quantum many-body systems modeled by Luttinger liquid theory, coupled via a time-dependent tunneling interaction $J(t)$.
key_observables: Logarithmic negativity (LN), mutual information (MI), Rényi entropies ($S_\alpha$), and entanglement entropy.
important_parameters: Temperature ($ eta$), coupling protocol function $J(t)$, and the time evolution regime (early-time, long-time average, adiabatic limit).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a Gaussian approximation for the interaction term and assumes initial states are thermal and factorized across the two fields.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates field-space entanglement generation via global coupling. Figure 2 summarizes the mathematical framework involving symplectic propagators and mode decomposition.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the model Hamiltonian, deriving the decoupled dynamics in terms of harmonic oscillators governed by the Ermakov equation, and then applying this formalism to calculate specific information-theoretic quantities (LN, MI) across various quench protocols and temperature regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous analytical tools for quantifying non-equilibrium quantum correlations in 1D systems, directly applicable to understanding entanglement generation in cold atom or superconducting circuit quenches.
